head: AT&T landline in California: FCC backs plan to end copper phone lines
dek: The FCC has overruled California rules that made AT&T get the state's approval before ending old copper landline service. AT&T has proposed ending that service in California on or after 1 June 2027, according to the state's utilities commission.
details: The FCC kept California's carrier-of-last-resort rules in place for now; AT&T is also suing the state over them, and that case is still open. Copper lines serve about 3% of California households, according to the FCC. AT&T says it wants to put its money into fiber and 5G, and some residents worry that patchy cell service would be their only option. It's not yet clear whether AT&T will go ahead with the phase-out.
where: California, AT&T copper landline customers; earliest date 1 June 2027
means: If you have an AT&T landline on copper in California, it may be switched off from mid-2027, so you'd need another way to call, including for 911.
todo: Nothing to do yet. Check whether fiber or good cell coverage reaches your home, and watch for letters from AT&T about your line.
